# **How to Accept Insurance as a Doula Without Changing How You Practice**


If you've held off on accepting insurance because you didn't want your work to turn into paperwork, you're not alone.


The good news is that accepting insurance doesn't mean giving up control of your practice. You still decide how you work, who you work with, and how you care for your clients. What changes is the insurance side: eligibility, documentation, claims, billing, and payment.


Here's how accepting insurance actually works in California, what Medi-Cal pays for covered doula care, and how you can take insurance without taking on all of the insurance work yourself.


### **What changes, and what doesn't**


Let's start with the part that matters most.


Your practice stays yours. How you show up for clients, your approach to care, your relationships, and the way you run your business don't suddenly belong to an insurance company because you start accepting covered clients.


What does change is the back end.


If you're handling insurance on your own, there's more to manage: enrollment, credentialing, eligibility, claims, billing, follow-up, and denials. Depending on the clients you serve, you may also need to contract with individual health plans.


With Loula, your part is much simpler: you log the care you provide, we handle the insurance work behind the scenes, and you get paid.


The paperwork comes with accepting insurance. It just doesn't have to become your job.


### **Why accept insurance at all?**


Accepting insurance can make your care accessible to birthing persons who may not be able to afford private-pay doula care.


When insurance covers the cost, it can remove or significantly reduce the out-of-pocket cost barrier for eligible clients. In California, Medi-Cal covers doula care, and Loula also works with major commercial health plans, including Kaiser and Health Net.


That can mean reaching birthing persons who may not have found or been able to work with you otherwise.


And accepting insurance doesn't have to replace your private-pay work. It's another way to get paid that you can add alongside the practice you've already built.


### **How accepting insurance works in California**


There are two main sides to insurance-covered doula care in California: Medi-Cal and commercial health plans.


#### **Medi-Cal**


To provide covered care to Medi-Cal members, you'll need to meet Medi-Cal's qualifications and complete the appropriate enrollment process.


The basic steps include:


1. [Get a National Provider Identifier (NPI)](https://nppes.cms.hhs.gov/help/faqs-help-page) **.** Doulas need an NPI to enroll with Medi-Cal.
2. [Meet Medi-Cal's doula qualifications](https://www.dhcs.ca.gov/providers-partners/doula-services-frequently-asked-questions/) **.** You must be at least 18 years old, have current adult and infant CPR certification, and complete[basic HIPAA training](https://hipaatraining.us/#module1) . You'll also need to meet the requirements of either Medi-Cal's training or experience pathway.
3. **Gather your required documents.** What you need can depend on how you're enrolling and where you provide services.
4. **Submit your application through PAVE.** PAVE is California's Provider Application and Validation for Enrollment portal.


If you plan to serve Medi-Cal managed care members, PAVE enrollment isn't necessarily the end of the process. Managed care credentialing and contracting are separate, and doulas may need to contract with individual Medi-Cal managed care plans in the areas where they work.


#### **Commercial health plans**


Loula also works with major commercial health plans, including Kaiser and Health Net.


Each plan has its own requirements around credentialing, contracting, eligibility, covered services, and billing. If you're managing insurance independently, that can mean navigating a different process for each plan you want to work with.


With Loula, we handle the credentialing and contracting process with the health plans we work with, verify client eligibility, and manage the billing and claims on your behalf.


### **What does Medi-Cal pay doulas?**


For Medi-Cal fee-for-service, current published reimbursement rates include:


- **Initial visit, up to 90 minutes:** $197.98
- **Prenatal or postpartum visit:** $162.11
- **Extended postpartum visit, up to three hours:** $486.36
- **Labor and delivery support, vaginal delivery:** $685.07
- **Labor and delivery support, cesarean delivery:** $795.73
- **Support for miscarriage or abortion:** $250.85


For the standard set of covered services plus a vaginal delivery, the published fee-for-service rates can total up to about **$3,152** . Additional postpartum visits may also be covered when medically recommended.


Medi-Cal managed care and commercial plan payment arrangements can work differently, so what you're paid can depend on the plan and contract.


### **Can I bill insurance as a doula on my own?**


Yes.


You don't need Loula in order to accept insurance. You can enroll, credential, contract, and bill independently.


For Medi-Cal, that means completing the appropriate enrollment process and, depending on the clients you serve, managed care credentialing and contracting as well. You'll also be responsible for verifying eligibility, documenting covered services, submitting claims, following up on payment, and handling delays or denials.


**With Loula, you can accept insurance without taking on all of the insurance work yourself.** We handle that work behind the scenes while you keep running your practice.


### **The admin is real**


Insurance comes with real administrative work.


Enrollment and credentialing take time. Client eligibility needs to be verified. Claims need to be submitted correctly and followed up on when they're delayed or denied. Different plans can have different requirements, and those requirements can change.


None of that has much to do with why you became a doula, but someone still has to do it.


That's the part Loula takes on.


### **How Loula handles the insurance side**


Loula handles the parts of accepting insurance that have nothing to do with providing doula care, so you can keep your focus on your clients and your practice.


We handle credentialing and enrollment, and doulas can often get set up with Loula in about two to three weeks, and if you're already PAVE enrolled it should be even faster. We verify each client's coverage before care begins. You log the services you provide, and we turn them into claims, submit them, and manage the follow-up.


If a claim is delayed or denied, we handle it.


And you don't have to wait for the health plan to pay us before you get paid. Loula pays doulas on a dependable schedule, twice a month. Your payment stays on schedule while we handle the insurance side.


We work with individual doulas and doula groups, whether you're brand new to insurance or have been working with health plans for years. We can also connect you with insurance-eligible birthing persons looking for doula care.


You keep running your practice your way.


[Add insurance-covered care to your practice](https://joinloula.com/providers) , and leave the insurance work to us.


### **Frequently asked questions**


**How do I accept insurance as a doula in California?**


You can enroll and bill insurance independently or work with a partner like Loula. For Medi-Cal, doulas need an NPI, must meet[Medi-Cal's qualifications](https://mcweb.apps.prd.cammis.medi-cal.ca.gov/page/medi-cal-enrollment-requirements-and-procedures-for-doulas) , and can enroll through PAVE. Serving managed care members may also require separate credentialing and contracting with individual plans.


**How do I bill insurance as a doula?**


Once you're properly enrolled or contracted, covered services need to be documented and submitted to the appropriate health plan as claims. You'll also need to verify client eligibility and manage claim follow-up, including delays or denials. With Loula, you log the services you provide and we handle the claims and insurance follow-up.


**Do I have to change how I practice to accept insurance?**


Accepting insurance doesn't mean giving up control of your practice. You continue running your practice and caring for your clients, while meeting the eligibility, documentation, and billing requirements for covered services.


**How much do doulas get paid by Medi-Cal in California?**


Current Medi-Cal fee-for-service rates include $197.98 for an initial visit, $162.11 for a prenatal or postpartum visit, and $685.07 to $795.73 for labor and delivery support, depending on delivery type. Payment through managed care plans can work differently.


**How long does it take to get set up with Loula?**


Doulas can often get set up with Loula in about two to three weeks. Timing can depend on your circumstances and the plans you're enrolling with.


**When do I get paid if I bill insurance through Loula?**


Loula pays doulas on a dependable schedule, twice a month, without waiting for the health plan to reimburse us. If a claim is delayed or denied, we handle the insurance follow-up.


**Can I accept insurance and still charge privately?**


Yes. Accepting insurance is something you can add alongside your existing private-pay work. It doesn't have to replace the practice you've already built.
